title: Crispy Potato Hash with Eggs
summary: Cubed potatoes fried until crunchy with onion and bell pepper, then topped with eggs cooked right in the pan. Breakfast for dinner, done in one skillet.

creator.bio: Sample creator. American weeknight basics that feed a crowd and leave few dishes.

steps.instruction: Cut the potatoes into small, even cubes and pat them dry with a towel.
success_cues: Cubes are about the same size
Potatoes feel dry to the touch
warnings: Sharp knife: curl your fingertips under and keep the board steady on a damp towel.
steps.creator_note: Dry potatoes are crispy potatoes. Wet ones steam.

steps.instruction: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes in a single layer and cook without stirring for 5 minutes, then flip and cook 8 to 10 minutes more, turning now and then.
success_cues: Potatoes are golden and crisp on several sides
A fork slides easily into a cube
warnings: Hot oil can spit; add food away from your body and keep the handle turned inward.

steps.instruction: Add the butter, onion and bell pepper, salt and pepper. Cook 4 to 5 minutes until the vegetables soften.
Make four wells in the hash and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook on medium-low until the whites are fully set, 4 to 6 minutes.
success_cues: Whites are opaque with no clear, jiggly parts
Yolks are as firm as you like them
warnings: Runny yolks are undercooked eggs; cook longer until firm if you are serving young children, pregnant guests or anyone who avoids runny eggs.

steps.instruction: Scatter chives over the top if using and serve straight from the skillet.
success_cues: Each serving gets crispy potatoes and two eggs
warnings: The skillet handle is hot; use a mitt.

creator_notes: Leftover roasted or boiled potatoes work too and cut the cook time in half.
